title: Is <slot dir=auto> special case needed?

labels.name: i18n-tracker
labels.description: Group bringing to attention of Internationalization, or tracked by i18n but not needing response.

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#auto-directionality step 2 defines slot auto directionality in terms of assigned nodes.

Previously, a slot's directionality was used as strong resolution for ancestor `dir=auto` elements. But #9880 changed this to use the directionality of the slot's shadow root's host. The assigned nodes inherit their directionality through the light tree. Step 2 applies if there are assigned nodes, so default content is not relevant. Afaik, step 2 only has implications for the `:dir` selector.

The step comes with costs. One implication is that a text node in the light tree can be used by multiple slots in multiple shadow trees for `dir=auto` resolution ([test](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/871325b8460362073cb2069874bef7dde3170cb2/testing/web-platform/tests/html/dom/elements/global-attributes/dir-auto-dynamic-changes.window.js#276-306)). This specifically complicates the code in Gecko that keeps track of dynamic changes. If the step isn't needed, implementers could avoid unnecessary computations. Currently, there are two open bugs in Gecko related to step 2 ([bug 2015010](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2015010), [bug 2015828](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2015828)). The special case has already caused issues in the past, #10488.

Maybe #9880 should've removed step 2? Or is there a practical example for why it's needed?

Removing would mean slot auto directionality is based on default content. Alternatively, step 2 could also be to take the shadow root's host directionality.

@dbaron @zcorpan
